gloss: to humor someone; to try to please; to curry favor

definitions.gloss: to humor someone; to try to please; to curry favor with
definitions.explanation: To act in a way designed to make someone happy or to get on their good side, often by flattering them or doing what they want. Can have a slightly negative connotation of being insincere.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとる。
examples.english: To try to please one's boss.

examples.japanese: ⟦{怒|おこ}っている→怒る：00876_okoru⟧⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとろうとお⟦{菓子|かし}→菓子：00191_kashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧きた。
examples.english: I bought sweets to try to humor my angry girlfriend.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとること⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦{考|かんが}えている→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{言|い}えなく→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: If you only think about pleasing others, you won't be able to express your own opinions.

notes:
⟦{機嫌|きげん}→機嫌：02367_kigen⟧ means mood or humor, and とる here means to take or handle. The expression describes actively trying to manage or improve someone else's mood.

The expression can be neutral (comforting a child) or slightly negative (being obsequious to a superior). Context determines the nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとる (to humor one's boss)
- {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとる (to soothe a child's mood)
- ⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{機嫌|きげん}をとる (to please a customer)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {機嫌|きげん}をとる: to try to please, to humor (general)
- ⟦ご{機嫌|きげん}→ご機嫌：25581_gokigen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{取|と}り{結|むす}ぶ: to curry favor (more formal, literary)
- ⟦{媚|こ}びる→媚びる：09028_kobiru⟧: to flatter, to fawn (stronger negative connotation)
- ⟦{胡麻|ごま}→胡麻：10337_goma⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to butter up (colloquial, idiomatic)
